minutes.headline: Open Space Committee backed waiving the town's right of first refusal on five Holmen Street lots; chair to step down
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed a Chapter 61 notice of intent to sell five lots from a larger forest parcel on Holmen Street. It agreed to recommend not exercising the town's right of first refusal. It also heard of a donation from Bright Farms to an open space account and the chair's plan to step down. It set a December meeting and a November site visit to Lake Shirley parcels.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted by roll call to recommend that the town waive its right of first refusal on the Holmen Street Chapter 61 sale.
The notice covers five lots from a larger forest parcel. The town has 120 days to act and would step into the buyer's role if it did.
The committee heard that Bright Farms gave a donation to an open space account after withdrawing its greenhouse project.
The chair plans to step down, and Mike will chair the next meeting, at which a new chairperson is to be appointed.
The committee set a Lake Shirley site visit and put the tax title process for those parcels on the December agenda.

why_it_matters: Recommending against first refusal means the town is not expected to buy the Holmen Street forest land, so the sale to a private buyer can go ahead and the land leaves the Chapter 61 program's protection.
Any move on the Lake Shirley parcels would need funding from the select board, so a request may come to a later vote.
